title: Flora and Rusty's Singing Stones
markdown:
There are big green meadows that stretch out like soft blankets under the sun. In one meadow, a little while ago, lived a little fawn named Flora. Flora had tiny legs, a tail that twitched like a busy butterfly, and eyes as big and brown as acorns. She loved her meadow, oh yes. But some days, even sunny days, felt a little the same. The buttercups looked the same, the daisies were always white with yellow middles, and the sound of leaves was all she heard.

“Hmmph,” Flora sighed. She nudged a round dandelion with her soft nose. “Another nice day. And nice means a little bit boring.” She kicked her little hoof against a clump of clover. It tickled her toes, but it didn’t make her feel better. She wished for something surprising, something that would make her eyes grow wide.

Beside her, a warm rumble shook the ground. It was Rusty, a farm dog with fur the colour of toast and a tail that never stopped wagging. Rusty didn’t always know what Flora’s sighs meant, but he knew friendship. He nudged her gently with his wet nose. His tail gave a happy thump-thump-thump on the grass.

“Woof?” he asked. That meant, What’s wrong, friend? Are you a little sad? Can I help?

“Oh, Rusty,” Flora said, her voice as soft as a summer breeze. “I just wish we could find something new. Something surprising. Something that makes us giggle.” She looked up at Rusty with her big kind eyes.

Flora and Rusty walked to the edge of their meadow. A little stream went gurgly-gurgly there. It whispered secrets to the smooth grey stones. The water sparkled like tiny diamonds in the sun. Little silvery fish darted fast. Rusty loved to splash in the stream. Flora liked to watch the quick fish. But the stream was a little wide. It was a playful barrier between their meadow and… well, what was on the other side?

“Look, Rusty,” Flora pointed with her nose. Her dappled fur seemed to shimmer with new interest. Beside the water, peeking out from soft green moss, was a special stone. It was round and flat, with a swirly pattern on it. It looked a little bit like a tiny seashell, all creamy white and pale green. It felt special, like it had a secret.

“Woof,” Rusty barked, sniffing it. His nose twitched. It smelled like sunshine and damp earth, but also something new and exciting.

Flora tilted her head. Her long ears twitched. “I’ve never seen this stone before. It looks friendly. It looks like it wants to tell us something.” She tapped it gently with her hoof. Nothing. She nudged it. Still nothing. “It’s just a stone,” she said, a little sigh escaping. She had hoped it was a magic stone that could make a bridge.

Then a fun idea popped into Flora’s head, like a little bubble from the stream. “Rusty,” she whispered, her voice full of wonder, “what if we sang to it? A really happy song.”

Rusty’s tail gave a mighty wag. He wiggled with glee. He loved to sing. Well, he loved to bark tunelessly with all his heart. That was his best singing. He let out a happy arf that showed his excitement.

“Okay,” Flora said, puffing out her chest. “Let’s try. Together. A happy song about our meadow and our friendship.” She started to hum a little tune, a cheerful bouncy melody. Rusty joined in with happy barks and excited woofs. His tail was a blur.

“La-la-la, meadow so bright,
Friends together, pure delight.
Woof-woof-woof, happy and free,
Sing a song for you and me.”

And wouldn’t you know it? As their happy song filled the air, a soft golden light began to glow from the mossy stone. It pulsed gently, like a little sun waking up. Then, with a soft pop, a second stone, just like the first, appeared beside it. And another. And another. A perfect shimmering line of singing stones stretched right across the stream, leading to the other side.

“Oh, Rusty,” Flora gasped. Her eyes were wide with amazement. “It worked. Our song made the path. The stones heard our happy tune.”

They looked at each other. Their eyes sparkled with wonder. This was new. This was surprising. This was just what Flora had wished for.

“Let’s go,” Flora said, her boredom all gone. With a skip, she hopped onto the first singing stone. It felt warm and solid. Rusty followed, his paws making soft thuds. His tail still wagged with excitement. Their song grew louder as they crossed. Their happy song of friendship and discovery echoed over the stream.

The singing stone path didn’t just lead them to the other side of the stream. It led them to a part of the meadow they had never, ever seen. It was a small clearing, bathed in wonderful dappled sunlight. And growing there was a patch of the plumpest, most purple, most juicy berries. They looked like tiny shiny jewels on green leaves. Each one was fat and inviting.

“Wow,” Flora breathed. Her soft nose twitched with delight. She took a little nibble. “Oh, Rusty, these are delicious. Truly, the best berries ever.” The taste was like sunshine and honey and a hint of summer rain.

Rusty agreed with happy grunts and satisfied slurps. His tail thumped a merry rhythm. They ate and ate. Their tummies grew happily full. Their hearts were full of joy from finding such a wonderful secret place, a place made just for them by their song.

“Our song showed us the way,” Flora said, licking a purple smudge from her lips. “The singing stones and the yummy berries. It was like a secret path just for us.”

The sun, bless its golden heart, doesn’t stay high in the sky forever. It likes to take a gentle rest. As Flora and Rusty finished their berry feast, their tummies round and content, they saw the sunlight begin to grow longer. Long gentle shadows stretched across the grass. The sky began to turn soft shades of pink and orange.

“Oh my,” Flora said softly. Her ears drooped just a tiny bit. “It’s getting late, Rusty. We should go home before it gets dark.” The thought of home, of their cosy beds, made them feel a little bit sleepy.

They turned back towards the stream, ready to hop across. But where were the singing stones? The magic path had vanished. All they could see was the water, still whispering, but with no stones to carry them. Their side of the stream seemed quite far away now.

Flora’s ears drooped more. Rusty let out a soft whine, a questioning sound. How would they get back? The meadow, which had seemed friendly and full of surprises, now felt a little bit far from home. They sat on the soft grass, side-by-side, feeling thoughtful. The shadows grew longer. The world felt quieter.

Flora looked at Rusty. Rusty looked at Flora. They weren’t scared, no, not really. The meadow was still safe and warm. But they missed their cosy spots in the meadow, and the familiar sights and smells of home. That happy feeling from the berry patch began to fade a little.

Then Flora’s big brown eyes lit up, like a tiny spark catching a breeze. A little flicker of hope. “Rusty,” she said, her voice bright again. “The song. The path appeared because we sang. Maybe it will appear again if we sing.”

Rusty’s tail gave a hopeful thump. He nudged Flora.

Flora stood up. Her dappled coat gleamed in the soft light of the setting sun. She took a deep breath, filling her lungs with the sweet berry-scented air. She began to sing, her voice clear and sweet, carrying over the whispering stream:

“Singing stones, oh singing stones,
Show us the way to our homes.
Our song, our song,
Friendship’s tune, clear and strong,
Our song, our song,
Help us cross where we belong.”

Rusty joined in with his happy woofs and excited barks. He barked the song’s rhythm with his tail. As their voices blended, a soft hum filled the air. The stream shimmered. And there, one by one, the singing stones reappeared. They were solid and warm, forming their magic path across the water once more.

“Hooray,” Flora said. Rusty barked his happy agreement, his whole body wiggling.

With light hearts and wagging tails, they scampered back across the singing stones. They reached their own meadow just as the sky began to blush with evening colours, painting the clouds pink and purple. They had crossed the stream, found a secret berry patch, and found their way home, all because of a song.

Flora the fawn and Rusty the farm dog snuggled down in the soft meadow grass, side-by-side. They watched the first stars begin to twinkle. Tomorrow, if the meadow felt a little the same, they already knew the tune.
